# Command reference

<!-- Generated by docs/hooks.py from the live CLI. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command below is **stable** under the CLI compatibility policy from
0.7.0. Stable describes the contract, not a claim that 0.7.0 is released.
The Python API remains experimental until 1.0. See
[Public API and compatibility](public-api.md) and [Usage](usage.md).

Library commands accept `--file` / `-f` as an alternative to the first
positional library path. When one `.bib` exists in the working directory,
commands that read a library can detect it. Optional operands are shown
in brackets, and repeatable arguments end in `...`.

## Global options

**Stability: stable**

Reference management engine for BibTeX, BibLaTeX, and their materials

`pynakes [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--version, -V` | boolean | no | false | — | Show the pynakes version and exit. |
| `--install-completion` | boolean | no | null | — | Install completion for the current shell. |
| `--show-completion` | boolean | no | null | — | Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation. |

## analyze

**Stability: stable**

Describe a bibliography: what it holds and how complete its records are.

`pynakes analyze [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `--section` | list[choice] | no | — | entries, types, years, authors, venues, identifiers, fields, groups, lint, materials | Report only these sections (repeatable; default: all) |
| `--top` | integer | no | 10 | — | Length of the author and venue frequency lists |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## asset check

**Stability: stable**

Validate linked-file references (accepts multiple files for CI gating).

`pynakes asset check FILES... [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILES` | list[string] | yes | — | — | One or more .bib files |
| `--root` | list[string] | no | null | — | Additional directory to resolve relative linked-file paths; can be repeated |
| `--strict` | boolean | no | false | — | Exit 1 when a linked file is missing, unresolved, or the wrong type (for CI and pre-commit gating) |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |

## asset fetch

**Stability: stable**

Download Pinax materials, optionally using existing institutional network access.

`pynakes asset fetch [FILE] [TARGET] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `TARGET` | string | no | — | — | Citation key to fetch (default: all entries with configured missing materials) |
| `--material` | list[choice] | no | null | preprint, published, source, supplement, best-pdf | Material to fetch, repeatable; overrides the library's pinax-fetch-policy. best-pdf is the published PDF when open access, otherwise the preprint; supplement fetches one unambiguous supplementary PDF |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--expect-sha256` | string | no | null | — | Refuse with an exit-2 ExternalModification conflict, writing nothing, unless the file's sha256 still equals this value: pass back the source_sha256 a --dry-run reported, so an edit made in between is never overwritten |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show what would be fetched without downloading |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff |
| `--cache-file` | string | no | null | — | Keep provider responses in a reusable cache file at this path (safe to delete or .gitignore). Omit it and nothing is written to disk: responses are reused for this run only |
| `--access` | choice | no | null | open, institutional | Publisher access context: open or institutional (uses existing network access); default: the library's pinax-fetch-access setting, else open |
| `--discover, --no-discover` | boolean | no | null | — | When a preprint is needed and the entry has a DOI but no arXiv id, look one up (OpenAlex, then Semantic Scholar), check it against arXiv's record, and use and record a confirmed id (eprint, only when the entry has none); default: the library's pinax-discover-arxiv setting, else off |
| `--progress` | choice | no | "auto" | auto, jsonl, none | Progress while the run lasts: auto (a bar on a terminal, nothing with --json), jsonl (one JSON event per line on stderr, also with --json), or none |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Select entries with the shared --where grammar: predicates joined by and/or/not, e.g. 'year >= 2025 and type in [article, inproceedings]'. Operators: contains, =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in [..], matches, ~ (fuzzy), exists, missing; 'used'/'unused' test the linked TeX sources and 'query NAME' runs a saved query. See `pynakes capabilities` for the full grammar. |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Select entries by citation key: comma-separated, repeatable. Shorthand for --where 'key in [..]', and narrows a --where given alongside it. |
| `--strict` | boolean | no | false | — | Exit 1 when a requested material failed to download or was unavailable (materials already present pass) (for CI and pre-commit gating) |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## asset repair

**Stability: stable**

Reconcile the Pinax manifest with the material files that exist.

`pynakes asset repair [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write manifest.json.bak (or the next free .bak.N) before reconciling |
| `--reclassify` | boolean | no | false | — | Also move each published PDF that `asset check` reports as misclassified (a preprint, on recorded evidence) to the preprint path, with its manifest record |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Report the repairs without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff of the manifest |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## convert

**Stability: stable**

Convert a library between BibTeX/BibLaTeX dialects and interchange formats.

`pynakes convert [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the input file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `--to` | choice | no | null | biblatex, bibtex, csl-json, ris, mods, endnote, csv | Target: a dialect (converted in place) or an interchange format (exported) |
| `--from` | choice | no | null | csl-json, ris, mods, endnote | Import the input from this interchange format to BibTeX |
| `--out` | string | no | null | — | Write export/import output here instead of stdout (- for stdout) |
| `--force` | boolean | no | false | — | Overwrite the output file if it already exists |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show changes without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff of the library, or of the --out file |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--expect-sha256` | string | no | null | — | Refuse with an exit-2 ExternalModification conflict, writing nothing, unless the file's sha256 still equals this value: pass back the source_sha256 a --dry-run reported, so an edit made in between is never overwritten |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## corpus combine

**Stability: stable**

Combine several .bib files into one (optionally deduping by citation key).

`pynakes corpus combine INPUTS... [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INPUTS` | list[string] | yes | — | — | Two or more .bib files to combine |
| `--out` | string | yes | null | — | Path to write the combined .bib |
| `--force` | boolean | no | false | — | Overwrite the output file if it already exists |
| `--dedupe` | boolean | no | false | — | Collapse entries that share a citation key; differing same-key entries are reported as a conflict instead of guessing |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Keep only the entries matching this selector in the combined output |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Keep only these citation keys in the combined output: comma-separated, repeatable. Narrows --where when both are given |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show what would change without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff of the output |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |

## corpus split

**Stability: stable**

Combine inputs, then route entries into several outputs by predicate.

`pynakes corpus split INPUTS... [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `INPUTS` | list[string] | yes | — | — | One or more .bib files (merged in memory) |
| `--route` | list[string] | yes | null | — | Output rule FILE='predicate' (repeatable). Predicate: any --where expression (including and/or/not), or one of * / used / unused / group "Name". used/unused read --tex/--aux, else the linked tex-sources. |
| `--force` | boolean | no | false | — | Overwrite the output file if it already exists |
| `--copy` | boolean | no | false | — | Send an entry to every matching bucket (default: first match only) |
| `--minimal` | boolean | no | false | — | Drop jabref-meta/pynakes-meta blocks and skip Pinax materials in outputs, for standalone single-entry or few-entry snippets |
| `--tex` | list[string] | no | null | — | TeX file(s)/dir(s) feeding the used/unused predicates |
| `--aux` | list[string] | no | null | — | AUX file(s)/dir(s) feeding the used/unused predicates |
| `--dedupe` | boolean | no | false | — | Dedupe by citation key while merging the inputs |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show what would change without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff of each output |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |

## enrich

**Stability: stable**

Conservatively fill missing metadata (modifies the file).

`pynakes enrich [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| `--published` | boolean | no | false | — | Also promote preprints to their published version, writing the published DOI/journal when one is available (requires --online) |
| `--only-field` | list[string] | no | null | — | Apply only updates to these fields (repeatable or comma-separated; 'type' for an entry-type change), e.g. --only-field eprint,archiveprefix after reviewing a --dry-run |

| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--expect-sha256` | string | no | null | — | Refuse with an exit-2 ExternalModification conflict, writing nothing, unless the file's sha256 still equals this value: pass back the source_sha256 a --dry-run reported, so an edit made in between is never overwritten |

| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## lint

**Stability: stable**

Validate entries and report issues (accepts multiple files for CI gating).

`pynakes lint FILES... [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILES` | list[string] | yes | — | — | One or more .bib files |
| `--strict` | boolean | no | false | — | Exit 1 when any finding is left after lint-ignore, --ignore, and ignore directives (for CI and pre-commit gating) |
| `--category` | list[choice] | no | — | correctness, content, formatting, consistency, profile | Report only these categories (repeatable) |
| `--ignore` | list[string] | no | — | — | Leave out a finding type (missing_doi) or a whole category (consistency); repeatable, and added to the library's lint-ignore setting |
| `--only` | list[string] | no | — | — | Report only these finding types (duplicate_key, missing_doi, ...): comma-separated, repeatable |
| `--severity` | choice | no | "info" | error, warning, info | Report only findings at least this severe: error, warning, or info (all) |
| `--summary` | boolean | no | false | — | Report counts (by severity, category and type) without listing each finding; the omitted count is reported as issues_omitted |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |

## metadata adopt-jabref

**Stability: stable**

Start maintaining a JabRef metadata projection for this library.

`pynakes metadata adopt-jabref [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--expect-sha256` | string | no | null | — | Refuse with an exit-2 ExternalModification conflict, writing nothing, unless the file's sha256 still equals this value: pass back the source_sha256 a --dry-run reported, so an edit made in between is never overwritten |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show changes without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## normalize

**Stability: stable**

Normalize entries: titles, authors, journals, DOIs, identifier case, and ordering.

`pynakes normalize [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `--title-protection` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Brace-protect capitalization-sensitive title words |
| `--title-field` | list[string] | no | null | — | Title-like field to brace-protect; can be repeated |
| `--term` | list[string] | no | null | — | Additional exact title term to brace-protect; can be repeated |
| `--drop-field` | list[string] | no | null | — | Field to remove from every entry (e.g. abstract); can be repeated. Off by default; combines with any normalize-drop-fields metadata key |
| `--author-style` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, biblatex, bibtex, conservative, jabref, none | Author-list style |
| `--journal-style` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, abbreviated, full, none | Journal-name style (default: no change unless metadata sets it) |
| `--journal-source` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, jabref, none | Base exact-mapping journal table, applied before --journal-table (default: jabref) |
| `--journal-table` | string | no | null | — | CSV/TSV with title, abbreviation, and optional ISSN mappings |
| `--ltwa-table` | string | no | null | — | CSV/TSV LTWA word abbreviation table |
| `--doi-normalization` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Strip DOI URL prefixes and labels down to the bare DOI |
| `--pages` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Rewrite page ranges to start--end |
| `--months` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Rewrite bare month names to BibTeX month macros (month = june -> jun) |
| `--invisible-characters` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Remove characters that render as nothing (zero-width spaces, stray BOMs) |
| `--key-generation` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Regenerate citation keys from the library's key pattern |
| `--identifier-case` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Lowercase entry types and field names |
| `--metadata-formatting` | choice | no | "metadata" | metadata, on, off | Consolidate metadata layout: pynakes-meta top, jabref-meta bottom |
| `--sort-by` | list[string] | no | null | — | Sort entries by a BibTeX field name; repeat for secondary keys (e.g. --sort-by author --sort-by year:desc). Use "citationkey" (or "key") for the citation key and append ":desc" for descending. "original" keeps the current order. Omit to follow the file's configured sort order. |
| `--only` | list[string] | no | null | — | Run only these steps, comma-separated and repeatable: metadata, drop-fields, invisible-characters, titles, authors, dois, pages, journals, save-actions, months, identifier-case, sort, keys |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Select entries with the shared --where grammar: predicates joined by and/or/not, e.g. 'year >= 2025 and type in [article, inproceedings]'. Operators: contains, =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in [..], matches, ~ (fuzzy), exists, missing; 'used'/'unused' test the linked TeX sources and 'query NAME' runs a saved query. See `pynakes capabilities` for the full grammar. |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Select entries by citation key: comma-separated, repeatable. Shorthand for --where 'key in [..]', and narrows a --where given alongside it. |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show changes without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--expect-sha256` | string | no | null | — | Refuse with an exit-2 ExternalModification conflict, writing nothing, unless the file's sha256 still equals this value: pass back the source_sha256 a --dry-run reported, so an edit made in between is never overwritten |
| `--ignore-missing-tex` | boolean | no | false | — | Regenerate keys despite missing linked TeX sources; those sources are not rewritten |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## ref show

**Stability: stable**

Show one uniquely identified reference, or triage several at once.

`pynakes ref show [FILE] [KEY] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `KEY` | string | no | — | — | Citation key to display |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Summarize several references at once: comma-separated keys, repeatable |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Summarize every reference this selector matches, in file order (the shared --where grammar, saved queries and used/unused included); narrowed by --key |
| `--resolved` | boolean | no | false | — | Include fields inherited through crossref/xdata |
| `--abstract` | boolean | no | false | — | Include each abstract in the --key summary |
| `--select` | list[string] | no | null | — | Return only these fields under 'fields': comma-separated, repeatable. A selected field the entry lacks is null and listed in missing_fields |
| `--include` | list[string] | no | null | — | Also report what the library records outside the entry's fields: materials (Pinax files and file links), provenance (manifest records and directives). Comma-separated, repeatable |
| `--max-chars` | integer | no | null | — | Cut every returned text value to at most this many characters; each cut is listed under 'truncated' |
| `--limit` | integer | no | null | — | With --key or --where, return at most this many entries per page |
| `--cursor` | string | no | null | — | Resume a paged read: pass page.next_cursor from the previous page. Refused when the library changed since |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## scrub

**Stability: stable**

Write a copy of a library with its private content removed.

`pynakes scrub [FILE] [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `--out` | string | no | null | — | Path to write the scrubbed copy (required unless --check). Give the input path to scrub it in place |
| `--force` | boolean | no | false | — | Overwrite the output file if it already exists |
| `--drop-field` | list[string] | no | null | — | Additional field to remove, beyond the default private set: comma-separated, repeatable, '*' glob allowed (e.g. --drop-field abstract) |
| `--keep-field` | list[string] | no | null | — | Field to keep despite the default private set: comma-separated, repeatable, '*' glob allowed; --keep-field '*' keeps every entry field and scrubs only blocks and comments |
| `--keep-comments` | boolean | no | false | — | Keep free @comment blocks and % comment lines |
| `--keep-metadata` | boolean | no | false | — | Keep jabref-meta and pynakes-meta blocks |
| `--check` | boolean | no | false | — | Write nothing; exit 1 if any private content is found |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Keep only the entries this selector matches (the shared --where grammar): --where used releases just the entries the linked TeX sources cite |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Keep only these citation keys: comma-separated, repeatable. Narrows --where |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | no | false | — | Show what would change without writing |
| `--diff` | boolean | no | false | — | Show a unified diff of what was removed |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--backup` | boolean | no | false | — | Also write a <file>.bak copy before overwriting, or <file>.bak.1, .bak.2, ... when earlier backups exist, which are never overwritten (off by default; writes are already atomic and re-parse-validated) |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## search

**Stability: stable**

Search entries by free text, phrases, or field-scoped terms.

`pynakes search [FILE] QUERY [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE` | string | no | — | — | Path to the .bib file (default: auto-detect single .bib in cwd) |
| `QUERY` | string | yes | — | — | Search query: words/phrases, optionally scoped as field:term or field:"phrase". Pass "" to select by --where alone |
| `--in` | list[string] | no | null | — | Search only these stored fields: comma-separated, repeatable. The citation key and entry type stay searchable |
| `--select` | list[string] | no | null | — | Return only these fields under 'fields': comma-separated, repeatable. A selected field the entry lacks is null and listed in missing_fields |
| `--in-field` | list[string] | no | null | — | Deprecated, removed in 0.9.0: use --in to choose the fields searched and --select to choose the fields returned |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Select entries with the shared --where grammar: predicates joined by and/or/not, e.g. 'year >= 2025 and type in [article, inproceedings]'. Operators: contains, =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in [..], matches, ~ (fuzzy), exists, missing; 'used'/'unused' test the linked TeX sources and 'query NAME' runs a saved query. See `pynakes capabilities` for the full grammar. |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Select entries by citation key: comma-separated, repeatable. Shorthand for --where 'key in [..]', and narrows a --where given alongside it. |
| `--case-sensitive` | boolean | no | false | — | Match case sensitively |
| `--fuzzy` | boolean | no | false | — | Also match near-misses (misspellings, inflections) by similarity |
| `--abstract` | boolean | no | false | — | Print an excerpt of each result's abstract beneath the hit |
| `--limit` | integer | no | null | — | Maximum number of matches per page |
| `--cursor` | string | no | null | — | Resume a paged read: pass page.next_cursor from the previous page. Refused when the library changed since |
| `--max-chars` | integer | no | null | — | Cut every returned text value to at most this many characters; each cut is listed under 'truncated' |
| `--no-rank` | boolean | no | false | — | Keep raw file order instead of ranking by match strength |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
| `--file, -f` | string | no | null | — | The library to read, as an alternative to the leading FILE argument (default: the single .bib in the working directory) |

## verify

**Stability: stable**

Verify entries against authoritative metadata (read-only).

`pynakes verify FILES... [OPTIONS]`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILES` | list[string] | yes | — | — | One or more .bib files |
| `--online` | boolean | no | false | — | Fetch DOI provider metadata; otherwise only local checks run |
| `--published` | boolean | no | false | — | Also report preprints that now have a published version available (read-only; informational, does not affect --strict) |
| `--where` | string | no | null | — | Select entries with the shared --where grammar: predicates joined by and/or/not, e.g. 'year >= 2025 and type in [article, inproceedings]'. Operators: contains, =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in [..], matches, ~ (fuzzy), exists, missing; 'used'/'unused' test the linked TeX sources and 'query NAME' runs a saved query. See `pynakes capabilities` for the full grammar. |
| `--key` | list[string] | no | null | — | Select entries by citation key: comma-separated, repeatable. Shorthand for --where 'key in [..]', and narrows a --where given alongside it. |
| `--cache-file` | string | no | null | — | Keep provider responses in a reusable cache file at this path (safe to delete or .gitignore). Omit it and nothing is written to disk: responses are reused for this run only |
| `--concurrency, -j` | integer | no | 8 | — | Number of provider lookups to run at once during an --online pass (result ordering and applied updates are unaffected) |
| `--strict` | boolean | no | false | — | Exit 1 when verification finds warnings or errors (for CI and pre-commit gating) |
| `--json` | boolean | no | false | — | Emit machine-readable JSON |
